text:
asha: heads up — seeing a TP all-reduce tail latency spike on prod-2 for gpt-medium-8 (pipeline 2x4). traces: t-9843. Started ~2:15 UTC after last runtime kernel-selector roll. SLO violations creeping to ~0.8% on 99.9p (normally ~0.03%).
liam: interesting, did the kernel selector change the fused-reduce path? commit 4f7a2b3 was merged yesterday.
rachel: confirm — selector now prefers 'pack+async' kernels for large seqs, but iirc that increases message chunking for TP stages.
asha: attaching quick perf snippet from staging repro (8 GPUs, TP=2, PP=4):
```
# microbench_allreduce.py --world-size 8 --tp 2 --msg-distribution seq-len=2-1024
avg_allreduce: 0.42ms (baseline)
95p: 0.9ms
99.9p: 3.8ms  <-- spike
observed many small msgs (~6-12KB) interleaved with a few 128KB bursts
```
liam: small msgs explain ring inefficiency — ring has per-hop overhead; tree algo can win for many small messages due to log(N) steps. did you try NCCL_ALGO=tree?
asha: tried quick local: NCCL_ALGO=tree drops 99.9p to ~1.4ms, but average slightly up for large msgs. tradeoff depends on distribution.
mike: i ran trace-level flamegraph: https://perf.internal/runs/t-9843 — looks like KV cache fragmentation is sending many prefix-only updates from each microbatch. Batcher is emitting 6 microbatches per step with misaligned chunk boundaries.
rachel: that sounds like our batching heuristic patch (change to prefer smaller latency-aware chunks) created more microbatches for shorter seqs. we also recently changed kernel pad alignment from 256B->4KB which increased effective msg sizes for some kernels; could be interacting.
liam: hypothesis: selector changed kernel->padding increase -> some ops emit 4KB-aligned fragments; KV cache fragmentation causes many 8–12KB all-reduces; ring overhead per fragment dominates.
asha: quick repro commands i used:
```
# disable new selector, run controlled run
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy
python tools/serve_bench.py --model gpt-medium-8 --tp 2 --pp 4 --seq-distribution "short=70%,mid=25%,long=5%" --microbatch 6
```
mike: i also tried toggling batcher.max_chunk_tokens from 512->1024 and saw fewer microbatches, 99.9p dropped to 1.1ms even with ring algo.
liam: good signal — we have two levers: 1) algorithm (ring vs tree) and 2) batching/chunk alignment. both affect message-size histogram that NCCL sees.
rachel: can we capture an end-to-end histogram of per-step allreduce message sizes and per-call latency for a failing trace? i want to correlate kernel selection decisions with chunk sizes.
asha: uploaded a CSV to the trace: perf/internal/t-9843/msg_hist.csv (cols: step, stage, msg_size_bytes, count, latency_us). sample: "step32,stage1,8192,14,720"
liam: action items: 
- rachel: add quick opt-in flag to runtime to force NCCL_ALGO=tree and log hist for 1h.
- mike: run controlled repro with batcher.max_chunk_tokens=1024 and kernel_selector=legacy, collect traces.
- asha: open incident ticket and attach these microbench results + flamegraphs (inc#4672). infra-bot: created inc #4672 and scheduled 2h window for repro on prod-staging.
infra-bot: Incident #4672 created by asha. Assigned: eng-runtime @rachel, @liam. Window: 2026-03-18T10:00-12:00Z.
asha: one more note — we should avoid toggling NCCL algorithm by default; prefer making batching/kv-cache behavior more stable so ring remains efficient for the bulk of workloads. tree as a fallback in autoscaler when we detect many small messages.
mike: agree. i'll instrument a lightweight detector: if >40% of reductions <32KB for 30s -> switch to tree for that job.
liam: sounds good. i'll draft a small PR to kernel selector to emit the message-size histogram per job so we can make an informed policy.
rachel: thanks everyone — i'll start the opt-in job now and report back within the window. :thumbsup:
